biomarkers.name: KIT
biomarkers.prevalence: ~10-20% for activating mutations; copy-number gain/amplification also enriched
biomarkers.clinical_use: KIT inhibitor therapy may be considered for selected activating KIT-mutant tumors (best evidence for imatinib; activity is mutation-dependent)

biomarkers.name: NRAS
biomarkers.clinical_use: No standard approved targeted therapy; may support clinical trial enrollment

biomarkers.name: TMB
biomarkers.prevalence: Typically lower than UV-driven cutaneous melanoma
biomarkers.clinical_use: May contribute to generally lower response rates to immune checkpoint blockade than UV-driven cutaneous melanoma, but responses still occur

biomarkers.name: NF1
biomarkers.clinical_use: No standard approved targeted therapy; may support clinical trial enrollment

biomarkers.name: Structural variants / copy-number gains (CCND1, CDK4, MDM2, TERT)
biomarkers.prevalence: Common relative to sun-exposed cutaneous melanoma
biomarkers.clinical_use: Reflect characteristic acral melanoma biology; no routine biomarker-directed standard therapy solely on this basis

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Lentiginous proliferation of atypical melanocytes at dermoepidermal junction of palms, soles, or subungual skin

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Often less inflamed than UV-driven cutaneous melanoma, with lower TMB and, on average, less robust immunotherapy responses, although meaningful responses still occur
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Dermal reaction similar to other melanomas

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Melanocytes of palms, soles, and nail beds (glabrous skin including subungual unit)
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Neural crest — melanocytes at acral sites
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Melanocytic differentiation with same lineage markers as cutaneous melanoma; distinct anatomic subsite biology
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Same MITF-based cell state model as cutaneous melanoma but with distinct genomic biology — copy-number alterations/structural variants (including CCND1, CDK4, MDM2, TERT and KIT) are more common than UV-signature point mutations; KIT-enriched biology enables KIT inhibitor therapy in a selected activating KIT-mutant subset
